transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Rachel Kim (Praxis CISO); Marcus Holt (Praxis Head of Platform); Anika Mehta (Praxis Compliance); Diego Alvarez (Praxis SRE)

Summary (auto): quick posture scan to see if Redwood meets Praxis' evidence and log requirements. Discussed RBAC/SSO, Trust Center access, KMS, and data residency.

00:00 - Liam O'Connor: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through an assurance posture review. I'll hand to Priya for a quick tech slide, and then we can go into questions.
00:23 - Priya Shah: Hi all, thanks. Quick intro, I'm Priya on the solutions engineering side. We'll cover how Trust Center surfaces SOC 2 evidence, RBAC roles, and our audit log pipeline. Note: sometimes the transcript writes Redwood counsel instead of console, so, uh console basically.
01:05 - Rachel Kim: Great thanks. For context, Praxis is preparing for a combined SOC 2 + ISO 27001 assessment in Q3. Our blocker for vendor approval is: can you provide exportable, tamper-evident logs and a KMS integration that meets our key rotation policy? Also residency - we need EU at-rest residency for certain customer datasets.
01:40 - Priya Shah: Yep, understood. On logs: Redwood has immutable append-only audit logs with SHA hashes and retention policies. We provide streaming exports to S3, and we have a Syslog/Splunk connector. One caveat—our hosted offering keeps logs in the region of the deployment, but if you want EU-only we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated on a Frankfurt region.
02:15 - Marcus Holt: When you say "immutable" is that something we can validate? We need chain of custody for our auditor.
02:34 - Priya Shah: Good question. We expose a signed manifest with daily snapshots and a log digest you can pull. The auditor can verify digests, we also deliver a CSV export with event IDs. I'll show the trust center demo in a bit, that shows the signed manifest UI.
03:00 - Diego Alvarez: Quick followup—what's the latency for log export? We need near-real-time ingestion into our SIEM.
03:15 - Priya Shah: Typical ETL is sub-60s for streaming hook to S3 and then depends on your SIEM pickup. For larger bursts we do batching; there's a tuning knob. In Dedicated you can tune buffers for near real-time.
04:02 - Liam O'Connor: Also to add on routing, we have smart-routing so requests can be pinned to eu model variants and eu hardware, that helps with residency. But we should scope your exact datasets.
04:35 - Anika Mehta: On RBAC, we need role separation to ensure auditors cannot access production logs, and we want read-only reviewers to see evidence. How granular is the Trust Center?
04:55 - Priya Shah: Roles are pretty granular: org-admin, compliance-reviewer, infra-operator, app-owner. You can scope per-project or per-model. You can also add time-limited access links for external auditors. Some customers reported the UI shows Redwood counsel in transcripts, ignore that, it's console.
05:30 - Rachel Kim: SSO side — we are SAML via Okta. Any gotchas?
05:45 - Maya Chen: We've integrated with Okta for multiple customers. We support SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning. For audit we recommend provisioning reviewer groups so you can toggle access during audits.
06:10 - Marcus Holt: On KMS, we currently use AWS KMS with external key rotation and an HSM-backed policy. Can Redwood bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?
06:28 - Priya Shah: Yes, we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted there are options for customer-managed keys in some regions. For full HSM control you would go with Private deployment. We'll need to map the key policy: we support envelope encryption, and we can rotate keys monthly or per your schedule.
07:02 - Diego Alvarez: Does your signer for the log manifest use a separate key? We want separation of duties.
07:15 - Priya Shah: Logs use an audit-signing key distinct from data encryption keys; that can be scoped to the compliance team. We'll capture that in the evidence matrix.
07:40 - Rachel Kim: Ok, I want to call out a couple of specific audit checks: access review trails for privileged roles, MFA enforcement for console access, and retention of raw request payloads for 90 days. Can you map those?
08:01 - Priya Shah: Yes. We have RBAC change events, SAML logs for SSO sign-ins, and can store raw request traces for a configurable window. There are cost tradeoffs for long retention, we can show estimated egress/storage in the Optimize tool.
08:45 - Marcus Holt: About Private vs Dedicated—what's the ramp and cost delta? We're evaluating both given regulatory appetite.
09:00 - Liam O'Connor: Dedicated is quicker to provision and gives you predictable throughput and a customer-isolated pool. Private is more work up front — networking, VPC peering or on-prem — but gives full control for keys and residency. We'll send a side-by-side estimate.
09:30 - Anika Mehta: We also need the SOC 2 report. Can you share the Type II?
09:43 - Liam O'Connor: We will share a redacted Type II and an ISO control mapping spreadsheet. Action item on my side, I'll send both by Friday.
10:05 - [00:10:05] Rachel Kim: (muffled) there was something else — are there known exceptions or residual findings in your last audit we should be aware of?
10:22 - Liam O'Connor: We had a couple of low-risk findings around patch cadence for one non-prod cluster in 2025, all remediated and documented. We'll include the remediation steps in the evidence package.
11:00 - Priya Shah: Going back to logs—practical demo, so in the Trust Center you click into "Audit Logs" and you can filter by event type, user, and resource. You can click export and choose signed manifest. Here's a quick screen share... (screen share description omitted in transcript)
12:15 - Diego Alvarez: About tamper-proofing, are those manifests timestamped via an external time source? We need NTP-synced timestamps.
12:34 - Priya Shah: Yes we sign with a timestamp authority; manifests include an RFC3339 timestamp and a signature. If you want, in the workshop we can pull a sample signed manifest and walk it through verification.
13:05 - Marcus Holt: On data residency, do you support shard-level residency? For example, certain datasets must never leave EU.
13:20 - Priya Shah: We support per-project residency. If you choose Private or EU Dedicated, the data and logs for that project remain in the selected region. For hosted multi-tenant, you can approximate but not guarantee physical isolation.
14:00 - Rachel Kim: For ISO 27001 mapping we'll need a direct mapping to Annex A controls. Do you have an Annex A mapping?
14:15 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, our compliance team maintains an ISO Annex A mapping document. I'll attach that with the evidence.
14:35 - Anika Mehta: A couple practical questions — are audit logs encrypted at rest end-to-end, and is access to S3 export keys logged?
14:55 - Priya Shah: Logs are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys where applicable, and we record key-access events. We also support HSM-backed key storage in Private deployments.
15:28 - Rachel Kim: Can we get a copy of the log schema? Our SIEM team will need field names.
15:45 - Priya Shah: Yes, we'll include the schema and an example export. That's part of Priya's action item.
16:10 - Liam O'Connor: Quick note on retention and cost — Redwood Optimize can simulate retention cost for logs at 90/180/365 days so you can show finance.
16:40 - Marcus Holt: Are there any legal or contractual obligations around subpoenas or data requests? Like how do you handle government requests if data is in a shared region?
16:58 - Maya Chen: For hosted deployments, we follow our legal process; we notify customers per our contract and we can provide audit trail. For Private deployments, customers have more control over data and support requests, depending on contract. We'll route legal questions to the account team.
17:30 - Diego Alvarez: For the technical workshop, I'd like to validate a full chain: request -> model invocation -> KV cache behavior -> audit log event -> manifest signing -> S3 export. Can we walk that?
17:50 - Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll build a small repro flow in a sandbox account and walk the chain. That will also highlight where batching affects real-time visibility.
18:20 - Rachel Kim: One more question on RBAC: can role changes be time-limited and automatically revoked? We need that for auditor temp access.
18:35 - Priya Shah: Yes, Trust Center supports time-bound role grants and one-click revocation. We also have an audit trail of grants and revokes with reason fields.
19:10 - Marcus Holt: Any known integrations gaps? We use Datadog and Splunk primarily.
19:25 - Priya Shah: Splunk and Datadog are common; we have native connectors and event streaming. We'll include connector configs in the workshop packet.
20:00 - Rachel Kim: Regarding SSO provisioning, SCIM — will deprovisioning immediately cut sessions or just prevent reauth? We need immediate session termination for high-risk accounts.
20:20 - Maya Chen: SCIM deprovisioning removes the user from the group, session termination depends on session timeout and SSO provider. We offer an API to revoke sessions; in Dedicated/Private that can be wired to your IdP for aggressive session kill. We'll demo that.
21:00 - Diego Alvarez: Cost question—if we enable 365-day raw request retention and signed manifests daily, what kind of storage costs are we looking at?
21:18 - Liam O'Connor: We'll run the numbers with your request volume. Redwood Optimize will provide a per-month estimate; we'll calculate egress if you pull logs into SIEM frequently.
22:00 - Anika Mehta: For the evidence package, will you include test artifacts for auditors like proof of encryption keys and rotation history?
22:18 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, we provide key rotation logs, SOC 2 controls evidence, ISO mapping, and sample manifests. We'll redact where appropriate.
22:45 - Rachel Kim: Ok, this is helpful. Can we close with a quick recap and owners?
23:00 - Liam O'Connor: Sure. Recap: Redwood will send redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO Annex A mapping, Priya will prepare Trust Center RBAC demo and log schema, and we'll schedule the technical workshop to validate log flows and KMS integration. Praxis will confirm data residency scope and provide regulated dataset list.
23:25 - Marcus Holt: Works for me. Diego will be our SRE lead for the workshop.
23:40 - Diego Alvarez: Yep happy to do that.
24:00 - Rachel Kim: Good. One small nit — can you also include information about your continuous monitoring controls? That's something our auditor will ask.
24:20 - Priya Shah: We'll include a summary of our continuous monitoring (WAF alerts, anomaly detection, deployment guardrails) in the evidence bundle.
25:00 - Liam O'Connor: Final note, we'll open a trustcenter read-only link for your compliance reviewers so they can poke around before the workshop. Maya will own that.
25:20 - Maya Chen: I'll create a read-only reviewer group and invite Anika and Rachel by Friday.
25:40 - [End of capture]

Post-call notes: Participants requested sample signed manifest and log schema; Praxis wants EU residency guarantee for certain projects which triggers Private/Dedicated conversation. Agreed to run a tech workshop to validate end-to-end log + KMS flow.

Action items (restated):
- Liam: Share SOC 2 Type II (redacted), ISO Annex A mapping and control matrix - due 2027-05-21
- Priya: Prepare Trust Center demo screenshots, log schema, connector configs - due 2027-05-24
- Maya: Provision read-only Trust Center access for Praxis compliance - due 2027-05-22
- Diego/Praxis: Provide list of regulated datasets and residency constraints - due 2027-05-23

End of transcript.
